limitations: Ten adult macaques of both sexes include Macaca mulatta and Macaca fascicularis, aged 5.5-16.5 years. The paper does not provide an animal-by-species, sex, age, dosing, survival and assay manifest. Ten injected animals do not establish ten independent animals for every neuronal or glial endpoint.

Intravenous BrdU was 50 mg/kg, either once or daily for five consecutive days, administered between 09:00 and noon. Materials and Methods lists survival times ending at 72 days, whereas Results twice gives 75 days as the maximum. The reference injection for that discrepancy is not reconciled; neither value is silently selected.

BrdU and PCNA label DNA synthesis or cell-cycle-associated profiles; they do not continuously observe completed cytokinesis or a clone. PCNA was examined in sections from the same brains, not as a second independent animal cohort or a reported same-cell BrdU/PCNA lineage assay. Apposed doublets suggest, but do not identify, sibling relationships.

Early and later regional labeling is compared across sacrificed animals. BrdU-positive cells at the longest interval are not specifically identified as neurons. Label retention does not establish the survival fraction of a birth cohort, a neuron-specific lifespan, absence of rapid turnover elsewhere or absence of BrdU toxicity.

Neuronal double labeling was examined 32 days after the last of five injections in PFA-fixed 40-micrometre cryosections. Twenty nonadjacent sections were examined for each of NeuN and TuJ1; these are section counts, not independent animals. Exact biological replication, section sampling, denominators and uncertainty are not supplied for the reported averages.

BrdU/NeuN and BrdU/TuJ1 are alternative marker assays, not a reported three-marker identity for every labeled cell. The study reports neuronal colabels in GCL/SGZ and none in the other examined hippocampal regions; sampling and marker sensitivity do not establish absolute regional absence. Raw confocal stacks, optical section positions and segmentation have not been reanalysed.

Fluorophore reversal, omitted-primary controls and Figure 2c-d address staining and channel artifacts. They do not establish lineage, complete specificity or quantified sensitivity. Antibody omission is not a biological no-neurogenesis control, and no matched dose-control experiment establishes BrdU safety.

O4 or CNP double labeling used sequential black nuclear and brown cytoplasmic peroxidase signals in ethanol-fixed paraffin sections of 8 or 10 micrometres. Figure 3 shows 27-day single-injection examples. These preparations are distinct from the 32-day neuronal fluorescence assay; marker-positive morphology does not measure myelin formation or conduction.

Astrocyte generation is attributed to Eckenhoff and Rakic (1988) and Eriksson et al. (1998), not a newly reported GFAP assay in this experiment. Finding several phenotypes near one niche does not establish a shared multipotent founder, self-renewal or exclusive stem-cell lineage. The 1988 GFAP/autoradiographic assays are separately reviewed and do not trace a common founder.

The approximately 1,000 BrdU/TuJ1-positive cells per hippocampus is extrapolated from about two profiles per section, 40-micrometre sections and an approximately 19-mm external anatomical length. Scaling by an external 4.8-million-neuron estimate and dividing by five injections gives the provisional 0.004% per day. This is not a direct daily birth count or an unbiased whole-hippocampus stereological census.

Five-day cumulative labeling followed by 32 days of survival combines labeling opportunity, subsequent division, dilution, survival and marker expression. A single retained-label estimate does not identify production and death separately. The paper itself leaves lower production versus lower survival unresolved. No empirical edge weight or universal rate is assigned.

The roughly tenfold rodent comparison uses a separate published mouse study and external denominators. The paper acknowledges unmatched age, species, environment, labeling and survival procedures. Absolute-age and relative-age hypotheses were not compared in one matched design, and this series supplies no invariant primate-to-human scaling.

Bipolar morphology and radial or tangential orientation support a migration interpretation but do not track displacement, origin or a radial-glial guidance interaction. Nearby cells are not a clone, and anatomical resemblance to developing neurons is not an executed construction rule.

The replacement interpretation draws on separate human neuron counts and macaque synapse counts. Synapse-count stability is not a matched neuron census. This experiment measures neither paired births and deaths, feedback of population state, replacement identity nor the fraction of older neurons ultimately renewed.

No electrical, synaptic-output, learning or memory assay was performed. A possible cognitive role, stable-memory benefit or recovery mechanism remains untested. Labeling in this study does not require an injury or learning manipulation and does not validate the source card's necessary incoming assertions, weights or minimum carrier counts.

The paper does not provide an animal-by-species, sex, age, dosing, survival and assay manifest. Ten injected animals do not establish ten independent animals for every neuronal or glial endpoint.

Intravenous BrdU was 50 mg/kg, either once or daily for five consecutive days, administered between 09:00 and noon. Materials and Methods lists survival times ending at 72 days, whereas Results twice gives 75 days as the maximum. The reference injection for that discrepancy is not reconciled; neither value is silently selected.

BrdU and PCNA label DNA synthesis or cell-cycle-associated profiles; they do not continuously observe completed cytokinesis or a clone. PCNA was examined in sections from the same brains, not as a second independent animal cohort or a reported same-cell BrdU/PCNA lineage assay. Apposed doublets suggest, but do not identify, sibling relationships.

Early and later regional labeling is compared across sacrificed animals. BrdU-positive cells at the longest interval are not specifically identified as neurons. Label retention does not establish the survival fraction of a birth cohort, a neuron-specific lifespan, absence of rapid turnover elsewhere or absence of BrdU toxicity.

Neuronal double labeling was examined 32 days after the last of five injections in PFA-fixed 40-micrometre cryosections. Twenty nonadjacent sections were examined for each of NeuN and TuJ1; these are section counts, not independent animals. Exact biological replication, section sampling, denominators and uncertainty are not supplied for the reported averages.

BrdU/NeuN and BrdU/TuJ1 are alternative marker assays, not a reported three-marker identity for every labeled cell. The study reports neuronal colabels in GCL/SGZ and none in the other examined hippocampal regions; sampling and marker sensitivity do not establish absolute regional absence. Raw confocal stacks, optical section positions and segmentation have not been reanalysed.

Fluorophore reversal, omitted-primary controls and Figure 2c-d address staining and channel artifacts. They do not establish lineage, complete specificity or quantified sensitivity. Antibody omission is not a biological no-neurogenesis control, and no matched dose-control experiment establishes BrdU safety.

O4 or CNP double labeling used sequential black nuclear and brown cytoplasmic peroxidase signals in ethanol-fixed paraffin sections of 8 or 10 micrometres. Figure 3 shows 27-day single-injection examples. These preparations are distinct from the 32-day neuronal fluorescence assay; marker-positive morphology does not measure myelin formation or conduction.

Astrocyte generation is attributed to Eckenhoff and Rakic (1988) and Eriksson et al. (1998), not a newly reported GFAP assay in this experiment. Finding several phenotypes near one niche does not establish a shared multipotent founder, self-renewal or exclusive stem-cell lineage. The 1988 GFAP/autoradiographic assays are separately reviewed and do not trace a common founder.

The approximately 1,000 BrdU/TuJ1-positive cells per hippocampus is extrapolated from about two profiles per section, 40-micrometre sections and an approximately 19-mm external anatomical length. Scaling by an external 4.8-million-neuron estimate and dividing by five injections gives the provisional 0.004% per day. This is not a direct daily birth count or an unbiased whole-hippocampus stereological census.

Five-day cumulative labeling followed by 32 days of survival combines labeling opportunity, subsequent division, dilution, survival and marker expression. A single retained-label estimate does not identify production and death separately. The paper itself leaves lower production versus lower survival unresolved. No empirical edge weight or universal rate is assigned.

The roughly tenfold rodent comparison uses a separate published mouse study and external denominators. The paper acknowledges unmatched age, species, environment, labeling and survival procedures. Absolute-age and relative-age hypotheses were not compared in one matched design, and this series supplies no invariant primate-to-human scaling.

Bipolar morphology and radial or tangential orientation support a migration interpretation but do not track displacement, origin or a radial-glial guidance interaction. Nearby cells are not a clone, and anatomical resemblance to developing neurons is not an executed construction rule.

The replacement interpretation draws on separate human neuron counts and macaque synapse counts. Synapse-count stability is not a matched neuron census. This experiment measures neither paired births and deaths, feedback of population state, replacement identity nor the fraction of older neurons ultimately renewed.

No electrical, synaptic-output, learning or memory assay was performed. A possible cognitive role, stable-memory benefit or recovery mechanism remains untested. Labeling in this study does not require an injury or learning manipulation and does not validate the source card's necessary incoming assertions, weights or minimum carrier counts.

All main scientific text, Materials and Methods, and the captions of Figures 1-3 were read in the PMC full text; all three archived figure images were visually inspected. The separate publisher PDF, animal-level manifest, raw histological counts, optical stacks and analysis files were not obtained or independently reproduced.
